title: Salary and five or six shows a day
summary: He confirms $70 for seven-day weeks versus others' $125, played his solo five or six times daily in theaters, and lived on savings during idle stretches.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: One of the books I was reading said that this was the first three-trombone section at that time, but the book's aren't always right, I know. You said that when you first joined, your salary was $70.00 a week providing that the band worked seven days.
And you said that in one band you joined, everybody was making $125.00 a week. Was that the salary in Duke's band at the time you joined?
Yeah, that was the basic salary.

Everybody made the same thing except me. Well, of course, Hardwicke when he came. He didn't make $125.00 either. I don't know exactly what he made, but $70.00 was my salary. And if you worked two days, you got two-sevenths, and if you worked all week you got it all, but --
When you first joined the band, were they working every day of the week, or do you remember?

Mostly. Mostly every day. The only gripe I had really then was the fact they had no restriction on the number of shows. Now, I was playing this solo sometimes five and six times a day, plus all of the band music -- first chair in the band, and it was kind of hard. I couldn't see that. I never could see that from the first.
Five and six times a day would be what? Theater or --
Do you remember how long you stayed at that salary?

I think it was almost two years. As I say, I don't have all of my records, pay slips and stuff, but for a while I used to keep every one of them. And then they got misplaced when I'd like leave one house, or one home and cut out. And so now I hardly have any. But I have some books that statements are in. But that was the way it was. And you paid everything except your transportation. So, I distinctly remember one time when we left New York to go out

on a New Year's Day or a New Year's performance, and I think we stayed out there almost two or three months with no work. And we just layed around the town. And the next date was past there, so we didn't come back to New York. We were living -- all of us living in New York then.
Well, you said that when you joined the band you had some savings, so --
-- you survived that, but what about people who might not have had any savings. What did they do?

I don't know. I don't know. But you see, for instance, if you had -- I know I had about $7-800.00. And a meal -- you could go down to the restaurant and get a very good meal for 35¢ in those days. So, it lasted quite a little while. The rooms were a dollar, two dollars a night.
